newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe says it may defy world ivory trade ban.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe says it may defy world ivory trade ban.

text.p: Zimbabwe's environment minister said in an interview published on Monday that Zimbabwe will defy a world ban on ivory trade if it fails its bid this week to be allowed to sell ivory from its "excess" elephant population.

Environment and Tourism Minister Chen Chimutengwende said in an interview with the state-controlled Herald newspaper that Zimbabwe would not accept any compromise at a 10-day Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES) being held in Harare.

Zimbabwe, Botswana and Namibia have asked the conference ending on Friday for an exemption from the seven-year-old ban on ivory trade on grounds that their combined 150,000-elephant herd is excessive and not endangered.
They are backed by Japan but face fierce opposition from many Western powers, including the United States and France, which say reopening trade would put elephants at risk worldwide.
"Zimbabwe will go it alone and sell ivory without CITES approval rather than accept a compromise," Chimutengwende said. He was unavailable for further comment.
Zimbabwe could break the ban only if it found willing trading partners in or outside the 138-member CITES.
A vote on the issue, the hottest at the conference, is expected later this week.
